newsitem.title: USA: AML sees falling short of EPS estimates.
newsitem.headline: AML sees falling short of EPS estimates.

text.p: AML Communications Inc said Tuesday it expects to fall short of meeting estimates of earnings per share of $0.12 for the fourth quarter.

The company said in a release that according to First Call, analysts put estimates of earnings per share at $0.12 and $0.44 for the fourth quarter and fiscal year respectively, both of which the company believes it will "fall substantially short of meeting."
For the fourth quarter ending March 31, 1997, the company said it expects to report revenues of about $2.5 million compared with $2.6 million for the same three-month period last year.
The company said, however, that it expects to report a 100 percent increase in revenues to about $14 million for the fiscal year ending March 31, 1997, compared with $6.98 million for the prior year.

The company said that while it realized a substantial increase in revenue on an annual basis and measurable increases on a quarterly basis through the third quarter, sales of cellular products throughout the year have been indicating a declining trend.
The company said the sharp decline in revenue for the fourth quarter is a result of major cellular infrastructure suppliers producing more cost effective macrocell base stations.
It added that the decline was also affected by improved multicarrier amplifier-based microcells, which now compete directly with the company's multicarrier amplifier product line.

As a result of these improved macrocell-based stations, AML said, the cellular industry's slow transition from macrocells to microcells has "impeded the company's ability to sustain its revenue growth rate throughout fiscal 1997."

Nonetheless, the company said it was "encouraged" by future prospects as it continues to create unique solutions involving its technological strengths, product diversification and customer relationships.
